raw_response:
I have been farming this land in Quzhou my whole life. My father did the same, and his father before him. I know only one way to farm here: wheat in the cold months, corn in the hot months. Every family on our village does this. The land knows it too, after so many years.

I have about 12 mu. Same land for both crops — wheat comes off in June, I turn around and plant corn right after. No point thinking about other crops. I would not know how to sell them, and the grain station buys wheat and corn. That I understand.

For seeds I go to the village supply shop. They sell the hybrid corn — Zhengdan 958, same as always, same as the neighbors. For wheat I use Jimai 22, the variety that has done well for us here for years. I trust what I know.

Fertilizer I apply by feel and habit. Before planting I mix in phosphate and potash with some compound fertilizer, work it into the soil. For wheat I topdress urea in early spring when the plants start pushing again. Better to use a little more than have a bad harvest. A bad harvest means a bad year.

For water I pump from the well. Wheat needs it — before winter sets in, again in March when it joints, again at heading. Three or four times. Corn in summer catches the rain mostly, but if July is dry I pump once or twice more.

Pesticides I spray when I see problems or when neighbors say there is aphid or rust coming. Wheat gets sprayed a few times. Corn less.

I use the rotary tiller now. Easier on my back than the plough, and faster.
